page.layout: One printed page (left-hand part of the scan, framed by a decorative border). Running head at top; one text column with paragraphs; a catchword-like word "randi" is the last line of the column, not a catchword. No marginal notes on this page; a faint show-through from the facing page at right is ignored.

main_text.p: siquidem in meliorem Lapidem, hoc est, in tincturam Solis, abire debeat: quò respiciens Paracelsus in libro de generatione metallorum sive mineralium, ita scribit: Si Alchymistæ sulphur illud auri possent reperire, quemadmodum bene potest reperiri (inquit) IN ARBORE AU RI ETEJUS RADICE (Hoc enim scrupulus est ipsorum universalis: NON ALTERUM ILLUD) utiq;letari possent, &c.

Hæc igitur hactenus de auro Philosophico nostro, quod plæ-risque omnibus video ignotum, & hucusq; in observatum fuisse dicta sufficiant. Nunc sub finem Cheiragogiæ nostræ colophonis loco breviculâ ex Basilio Tincturæ Solis Philosophici, itemq; Lapidis Philosophorum præcipui, præpa-randi

page.notes: The text is set within a decorative woodcut border on all sides. Several words are doubtful in the scan: "in observatum" (possibly "inobservatum"), "breviculâ", "Tincturæ" and the italic Paracelsus quotation, where the underlining and the italic letters are blurred. The line "IN ARBORE AU RI ETEJUS RADICE" is printed as set, with a letter-spaced heading. Parts of the line "Si Alchymistæ" are faint.
